source.title: Induction in Both Directions: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning in Masked Diffusion Language Models

page_placements.theme: Induction-like copying in other modalities and non-autoregressive models

record.tranche_reason: Measures repeated-token induction with a repeated-versus-control log-probability score and analyzes its circuit; applies this to matched AR and absorbing-mask DLM models.
record.gate_note: The study tests synthetic repeated-token induction and its mechanism. It does not measure a training-loss bump or token-index loss gain alongside induction, natural-language in-context learning in large models, few-shot task learning, or training-data variation. The implicit-timestep experiments are outside the claim versions. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures repeated-random-token induction (repeated vs control log-prob gain) and dissects its circuit with ablation and QK/OV decomposition. It does this in a new setting: absorbing-mask diffusion LMs, compared with matched attention-only AR models. T3 fits better than T1 because the main object is a new kind of system, although the recipe is close to the original.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that absorbing-mask DLMs learn a bidirectional, direction-symmetric induction circuit: previous- and next-token layer-0 heads feed later induction heads that use Q- and K-composition to find the source and OV to copy it. Induction emerges abruptly and needs at least two layers. The DLM's advantage over AR comes from two-sided context access. The authors also conclude that DLMs causally use the global mask rate as an implicit timestep.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a repeated-token task and repeated-versus-control log-probability gain related to the original induction measurement. Adds bidirectional masked-DLM evaluation and circuit ablations/decomposition; does not measure token-index loss gains or a training-loss bump.
record.method_sensitivity: Induction performance changes with the visible local context around the mask: left-only DLM performance is at or below the AR baseline, while visibility on both sides improves DLM performance. The study also reports different emergence timing for DLM and AR models.

fits_no_version.finding: The DLM's induction advantage over AR comes from seeing both sides of the mask. Left-only DLM scores 2.23 nats vs AR 3.46; both sides visible gives 4.39 nats.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bidirectional models' induction strength depends on two-sided local context rather than a stronger one-sided mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: DLMs linearly encode the global mask fraction after layer 0 (R2 0.82-0.91), and patching it shifts prediction entropy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masked DLMs learn an implicit timestep without a timestep embedding (unrelated to induction heads).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 9th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: Evidence is limited to small attention-only models and synthetic random-token repeated sequences. The study does not establish that the circuit explains natural-language in-context learning or behavior in larger models. Induction emergence is described, but no coincident loss bump or token-index in-context-learning gain is measured.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported outcomes were left out. Results about the implicit mask-rate timestep and its probe/patching effects do not bear on the listed induction claim versions.

untested.parts: Larger models, models with MLPs, natural-language text; mechanism analysis is done only on folded no-LayerNorm DLMs, not on the AR models or the original LayerNorm DLMs.
Whether emergence coincides with a sharp token-index ICL gain and a loss-curve bump.
Entire version: large models, share of ICL, token-index loss.
Other model families, larger sizes, other diffusion objectives (e.g. uniform-noise), modalities.
Effect of training-data properties, and whether ICL persists; only the training objective differs between conditions.
Entire version; no sub-step or multi-transition analysis of formation.

missing.what: One-layer AR and DLM models stay near zero induction score; at least two layers are required
Behavioural (LayerNorm) DLM induction scores: L2 forward 4.13±0.17 vs reverse 4.07±0.25; L3 4.47±0.31. Folded models: 3.67±0.15 (L2), 4.64±0.09 (L3).
AR full-sequence final induction scores at L2/L3 (only the 3.46 left-only comparison is recorded)
Selected induction heads' source attention 0.25-0.70 vs ≈0.03 for the next-highest head; 4-5 induction heads per run
Ablating a ±2 neighbour head drops the score by only 0.4-0.7 nats, vs ~2 nats for a ±1 head
Induction robust to heavy global masking when ±2 neighbours are visible (4.31→4.71 at 90% masking); collapses to ~0.5 when neighbours are masked

record.verdict_notes: The mechanistic rows (r01-r24, r28-r34) come from folded no-LayerNorm DLMs; the behavioural rows come from LayerNorm models. The record's V4 limits_scope label on r26 was dropped: weaker left-only induction than AR does not qualify whether induction appears. Training on FineWeb-Edu is identical across conditions, so V5 bears only on the training objective. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The DLM circuit is analyzed in small attention-only models; the paper does not establish the mechanism in larger models or natural-language tasks.
The paper reports abrupt induction emergence, but does not measure whether it coincides with a sharp token-index in-context-learning gain or a bump in the training loss.
Large transformers, most in-context learning, and token-index loss gains are not tested.
The study compares matched attention-only AR and absorbing-mask DLM models at depths 1–3 and across seeds; it does not test other model families, larger models, other architectures, or modalities.
No comparison varies the training data or training setup to test their effect on induction formation or persistence.
Few-shot task learning and mechanisms other than repeated-token copying are not tested.
The study does not test whether induction formation comprises multiple temporally distinct transitions; its circuit analysis concerns pathway structure, not separate training transitions.

relationships.condition: Six small attention-only absorbing-mask DLMs (folded no-LayerNorm, L2 and L3), repeated random-token task
relationships.reason: Previous-token head ablation drops induction by 2.07-3.30 nats in every run (r03,r07,r11,r15,r19,r23). The own-pathway QK term reaches 2.7-8.3 logits versus others below 2.4 (r28). The OV path copies (r29). Score is near zero without matching neighbours and rises with them (r32-r34).
relationships.display_finding: Previous-token head ablation reduced induction by 2.07–3.30 nats in every run, and the head's own QK pathway contributed 2.7–8.3 logits versus below 2.4 for other pathways; the OV path copied tokens, while induction scores were near zero without matching neighbors and increased with them.

relationships.condition: Absorbing-mask DLMs, where the query position is a [M] token
relationships.reason: The circuit is not only previous-token composition. A next-token head is equally causal (drops 1.62-3.30 nats; r04-r24 next-token rows), and composition runs into both query and key, unlike AR key-composition (r28). OV top-1 copying holds for only ~1/5 of tokens (r29).
relationships.display_finding: Next-token head ablation reduced induction by 1.62–3.30 nats, with composition entering both queries and keys; OV top-1 copying held for only about one-fifth of tokens.

statements.correction: Training: FineWeb-Edu, 250k steps. Evaluation: synthetic repeated random tokens. Previous-token ablation drops across six folded DLMs: 2.07–3.30 nats; r03, L2 run A: 2.10 nats.
statements.problem: Calling these synthetic models confuses evaluation with training. The cited r03 alone gives 2.10 nats, not the six-run range.

statements.correction: Section 4.1: L1 AR and DLM models stay near zero; L2/L3 induction emerges abruptly after roughly 8–24k steps; DLMs transition earlier than matched AR models.
statements.problem: The study is cited through r25 but no result from it appears in the statement; its result does not establish positional-scheme or spectral-constraint sensitivity.

statements.correction: Attention-only transformers: 16 heads, d_model=512; absorbing-mask objective and bidirectional attention. Six folded no-LayerNorm L2/L3 DLMs: forward/reverse induction scores 3.54–4.85 nats.
statements.problem: The numerical result is correct, but these DLMs still use standard multi-head transformer attention. This study extends the objective and attention direction, rather than demonstrating a non-MHA architecture.
